r18-pm, step 1c: the Hipparcos-Gaia proper-motion anomaly.

For a star with no resolved companion, the Gaia DR3 RUWE says that something
is pulling the astrometry but says nothing about how far the star has moved
off a straight line.  The proper-motion anomaly does.  It is the difference
between the short-term DR3 proper motion and the long-term mean motion
between the Hipparcos and Gaia positions, and it is therefore a MEASUREMENT
of the orbital velocity change across that interval -- from which the
curvature of the track, and hence the displacement from linear propagation,
follows with one division.

Source: Kervella, Arenou & Thevenin (2022), A&A 657, A7, VizieR
J/A+A/657/A7/tablea1, matched on the Gaia EDR3 = DR3 source identifier.

Run: python3 harvest3_r18.py [--requery]
